chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, altogether from Abū Qatādah al-Qummī, from Abū Khālid al-Zubālī, who said:

When Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام was taken to al-Mahdī on the first occasion, he stopped at Zubālah. I was speaking with him, and he saw me grief-stricken, so he said to me: “O Abū Khālid, why do I see you grief-stricken?” I said, “How can I not be distressed when you are being taken to this tyrant, and I do not know what he will do concerning you?” He said: “There is no harm upon me. When such-and-such a month and such-and-such a day comes, then meet me at the first milestone.”

I had no concern except counting the months and the days until that day came. I went to the milestone and remained there until the sun nearly set, and Shayṭān whispered in my breast, and I feared that I might doubt what he had said. While I was in that state, I suddenly saw a dark mass approaching from the direction of al-ʿIrāq, so I went out to meet them, and there was Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام at the front of the caravan upon a mule.

He said: “Indeed, O Abū Khālid!” I said: “At your service, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.” He said: “Do not doubt; Shayṭān wished that you would doubt.” I said: “All praise belongs to Allah who delivered you from them.” He said: “Indeed, I shall return to them again; I will not be delivered from them.”

key_terms.أَوَّلِ الْمِيلِ: the first milestone, the appointed place of meeting
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Satan, who sought to induce doubt
key_terms.الطَّاغِيَةِ: the tyrannical ruler to whom the Imam عليه السلام was being taken
key_terms.الْقِطَارِ: the caravan or train of riding animals
key_terms.وَوَسْوَسَ: cast whisperings or insinuations into the heart

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim’s عليه السلام foreknowledge and his encounter with the Abbasid ruler?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام informed Abū Khālid in advance of his safe return from being taken to the tyrannical ruler al-Mahdī, and the event occurred exactly as foretold. It highlights the Imam’s certainty, Abū Khālid’s momentary inner struggle against doubt, and the ongoing oppression the Imam would continue to face from the rulers.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Abu Qatada, from Abu Khalid Al Zabaly who said,

‘When they proceeded with Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> to Al-Mahdi (the Caliph), for the first proceeding, he<sup>asws</sup> was lodged at Zubala. I discussed with him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> saw me as gloomy, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Khalid! What is the matter I<sup>asws</sup> see you as gloomy?’ So I said, ‘And how can I not be gloomy and you are being carried to this tyrant, and I do not know how his conduct will be with regards to you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem upon me<sup>asws</sup>. When it would be such and such a month and such and such a day, so meet me in the first mile’.

So there were no worries for me except that I counted the months and the days until it was that day. So I went at the mile, and I did not cease to be with it until the sun almost set, and there was the whispering of the Satan<sup>la</sup> in my chest, and I feared I might doubt regarding what he<sup>asws</sup> had said. So while I was like that when I looked at blackness which had appeared from the direction of Al-Iraq. So I welcomed them and there was Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, in front of the caravan upon a mule.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it you, Abu Khalid?’ I said, ‘At your<sup>asws</sup> service, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be doubting. The Satan<sup>la</sup> loves it that you doubt’. So I said, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> who Save you<sup>asws</sup> from them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is return for me<sup>asws</sup> to them. I<sup>asws</sup> will not be safe from them’.
